summary: This bill requires clinical trials approved by the National Institutes of Health to set and meet diversity goals for participant recruitment and retention based on race, ethnicity, age, and sex, and mandates public reporting of these goals and outcomes.

scores.thoughts: This bill focuses on increasing diversity in clinical trials by setting recruitment goals, requiring data sharing, and launching public awareness campaigns. This directly impacts the quality and accessibility of healthcare by ensuring treatments are effective across diverse populations, thus strengthening the overall public health system.

The bill authorizes $10 million annually for FY2027-2030 (total $40 million) for a public awareness campaign and related grants. This new discretionary spending would marginally increase the deficit to fund the bill's priorities, but the amount is negligible relative to the federal budget and the bill's core focus is unrelated to fiscal policy.

Section 3 requires a study on reimbursing out-of-pocket expenses, compensating participants for time, and updating anti-kickback rules to facilitate payments; other provisions reduce participant burden through alternative follow-up methods. This constitutes government-directed action to lower financial and logistical barriers to trial participation, though the bill's primary purpose remains clinical trial diversity rather than broad affordability reform.
